commit.message:
Stop definition list nesting short of the recursion limit

DefListProcessor.run calls parseBlocks on the definition content, which
can contain further definitions, so a document of flat term/definition
pairs without blank lines nests once per pair and raises an uncaught
RecursionError from only ~5 KB of input.

DefListProcessor.test now declines to run near the recursion limit, the
same guard BlockquoteProcessor already uses; the remaining markers are
kept as text.

Fixes #1700.

commit.message:
Fix dropped text in emphasis handling

Due to the way Python Markdown processes content, we must safeguard
against content placed into tails that we've already processed.

1. Built HTML elements we plan to replace ahead of time and place in
   the cache. They are built as the text is when they were processed.
   Each entry in the cache will contain the element, the region it
   replaces, and the anchor (position of next delimiter Python Markdown
   will before that that region so we can account for new index of the
   modified buffer).
2. While the cache is not empty, we will sometimes receive tail content,
   already processed tail content so we can identify and ignore them.
3. Now we just return the pre-built HTML elements until the cache is
   spent.

Fix a few more dropped text cases

- We missed some rule of 3 logic when porting the solution over from
  BetterEm.
- Add in placeholder protection logic that I thought wasn't needed here
  because we didn't use punctuation logic, but the same placeholder
  fix that is required in BetterEm is required here as well.

commit.message: Bump version to 3.11.3

Apply the CommonMark rule of 3 which we missed.

Rule of 3: an ambiguous delimiter cannot pair with an open delimiter if
the sum of the original lengths is a multiple of 3 (unless both are
multiples of 3).

3 existing test were changed. These matched the results of other
CommonMark parsers but not the official CommonMark implementation. These
other parsers missed a subtle interpretation of the rule of 3 that the
official implementation applies.

Fixes #1690

commit.message:
Avoid rescanning for a comment close after unclosed comments

`HTMLExtractor.parse_comment` searches for `-->` (or `--!>`) from each
`<!--` to the end of the raw data. When there is none, it passes `<`
through as data and returns `i + 1`, so the next `<!--` repeats the
same failing scan. A run of n unclosed comments therefore costs O(n^2):
`'<!--' * 32000` (125 KB) takes about 5 seconds to convert and 250 KB
takes about 22 seconds.

If no close exists after some position in `rawdata`, none exists after
any later position in the same string either. The parser now records
the string and position of the last failed search and skips the search
when it would start at or after that position. The string is compared
by identity so the record is never reused for different raw data.
Output is unchanged.

commit.message:
attr_list: preserve valueless attributes as provided

-   A list of known boolean attributes is incorporated (`markdown/serializers.py: BOOLEAN_ATTRIBUTES`), differing per output format — the XHTML list is the one from the XHTML 1.0 spec, the HTML list is from the HTML spec — and `download` is on neither list.
-   At parse time (`markdown/extensions/attr_list.py`), a valueless attribute is represented internally as `key=None`. When the attribute is assigned to an element, the historic `key="key"` behaviour is maintained _only_ for known boolean attributes of the active output format; any other valueless attribute keeps the value `None`, preserving what the user provided.
-   The serializer (`markdown/serializers.py`) renders a `None` value as the bare attribute name in both formats, and renders `key="key"` in the minimized form under `html` only for known boolean attributes — so explicit values are now preserved as provided for non-boolean attributes.
-   Knock-on fixes: `UnescapeTreeprocessor` skips `None` attribute values, and `fenced_code`'s `handle_attrs` (which shares the parser) keeps its historic treatment of a valueless config word as a flag using the key as its own value.

Fixes #1501

commit.message:
Fix quadratic-time id generation in toc extension

`unique` probes `base`, `base_1`, `base_2` and so on from the start on
every call, so with many headers that share the same text the n-th
header checks about n ids and the whole document costs time that grows
with the square of the header count.

Add an optional `counters` cache to `unique` which records, per base id,
how far the run of taken suffixes is already known to extend, and pass
one cache per document from `TocTreeprocessor.run`. The cache is only
used when the probe run is contiguous with it, so the result is the same
as the plain probe even when explicit ids leave gaps or an id such as
`foo_07` collides numerically but not as a string. Calls without the
cache behave as before.

commit.message:
Fix quadratic-time backtracking in hash header regex

`HashHeaderProcessor.RE` matches the header text lazily one character at
a time and, after each step, tries `#*(?:\n|$)` to see whether only
closing hashes remain. When the lazy match is inside a run of `#` that
is followed by more text, that check scans to the end of the run and
then fails, so a run of n hashes costs O(n^2). A line such as `# `
followed by 8000 `#` and an `x` takes about 13 seconds to convert. A
run of hashes ending in a backslash (`'#' * n + '\\'`) hits the same path.

Header text now consumes a run of hashes in one step when the run is
followed by something other than a newline or the end of the block, and
a lone `#` is no longer matched by the single-character branch. The
lazy match therefore only stops at the start of a hash run, never
inside one, and every match and capture group is unchanged. This was
checked against the old pattern on every string of up to 8 characters
over `#`, `\`, `a` and newline, plus random longer strings.

This differs from #1545, where the time was spent in inline escape
handling; here the time is spent inside the block regex itself.

Fix TOC labels for quoted HTML angle brackets

The TOC tag stripper stops at the first greater-than sign, including one
inside a quoted attribute. Attribute text then enters heading IDs and TOC
labels. Reuse the inline parser's HTML pattern to strip the complete tag
in both heading content and custom labels, preserving HTML entities.

Add regression coverage for both quote styles, embedded quotes, multiline
attributes, generated IDs, TOC tokens, and custom labels.

Assisted by Codex with investigation, implementation, tests, changelog,
validation, and this commit message.

Signed-off-by: Casper Verbuyst <casperverbuyst@gmail.com>

Fix quadratic-time backtracking in attr_list attribute regex

`AttrListTreeprocessor.BASE_RE` matched the attribute content with
`([^\}\n ][^\n]*)` and then allowed trailing spaces before the closing
brace with a separate `[ ]*`. Because `[^\n]*` already matches spaces,
the two groups both cover the same run of trailing spaces. When a block
ends with an unclosed attribute list, the closing brace is never found,
so for a run of n spaces the engine retries the match from each of the
n+1 ways to split the spaces between the two groups, which is O(n^2).

The trailing `[ ]*` can only ever match zero characters in a successful
match (the greedy `[^\n]*` consumes the spaces first), so dropping it
leaves every match and capture group unchanged while removing the
ambiguity. A two-line block such as `text\n{a` followed by 200k spaces
drops from ~10s to ~20ms, and the cost is now linear in the input size.

commit.message: Bump version to 3.11.2
Add checklist of parts to PR template

Update AI Policy

Explicitly require AI use disclosure and require use of PR & Issue templates when
provided. This should give us the justification to easily close all submissions that
are obviously autonomously submitted.

Sanitize attribute names in fenced_code and legacy_attrs

An attribute name supplied through the attr_list {attrs} syntax on a fenced
code block, or through the legacy_attrs {@name=value} syntax, was written to
the output without sanitization. The attr_list scanner permits a name of
[^ =}]+ and legacy_attrs permits [^}]*, both of which allow >, <, / and
quotes, so a name such as x><svg/onload=alert(1) closed the enclosing tag and
injected a live element. Reuse attr_list.sanitize_name, which the element path
already applies, at both sites. Valid names are unchanged.
Add fixed category to changelog

Revert enforcement of CommonMark punctuation rules

Some foreign languages are hindered by CommonMark style punctuation
rules. For backwards compatibility, revert enforcement of CommonMark
punctuation rules and leave that up to 3rd party libraries if desired.
Bump version to 3.11.1

Rewrite emphasis handling

- This is a complete rewrite of how emphasis handling is done.
- Drop use of multiple regex patterns in run in multiple passes and
  instead evaluate delimiters, nested or otherwise, and build up HTML
  elements.
- Try to consume tokens as much as possible until a full element is
  constructed (with children if any).
- If an outer set of tokens cannot be resolved, but one or more sub
  tokens can, render the first sub token span and cache the remaining
  ones for subsequent reentry and render those until the cache is
  exhausted.
- Two tests results were updated to match new behavior.
- If Markdown object is ever left in a bad state reset the stack.
This is a preventative measure to ensure the processor is always in a good
state. This situation has never been observed, but if it did occur,
this would allow the processor to reset its state and continue properly.
Only extensions have a way to reset, processors don't. Nor do they have
a way to detect when a reset would be needed.

- If an outer set of tokens cannot be resolved, but one or more sub

Fix inline HTML case

HTML handling is inconsistent. In some places it allows `<` and `>` in
attributes, and in other places rejects it.

The HTML spec allows for these in attributes, and browsers will escape
them. While it is generally recommended that users escape `<` and `>`,
it is not explicitly required.

If the attribute is quoted, it should allow `<` and `>`.

Update regex pattern to allow attributes with angled brackets and use
possessive quantifiers to performance as we are now only supporting
Python 3.10+.

commit.message:
Final cleanup for Zensical transition

- Add redirects for moved/renamed sections
- Implement and document manual result blocks
- Various other minor tweaks.
Add py-render custom code block formater

Fix quadratic-time backtracking when a reference link has no URL

A malformed reference definition line, one with a label but no URL
(just trailing whitespace after the colon), makes ReferenceProcessor's
regex backtrack badly. The pattern had two adjacent [ ]* groups around
an optional newline, both matching the same run of spaces, so for a
string of n spaces there were n+1 ways to split them before the engine
gave up and tried the next split. That turns markdown.markdown('[id]:'
+ ' ' * 50000) into an eight second call instead of a near-instant one,
and it gets worse fast as the input grows.

Rewrote the pattern so the leading run of spaces is consumed greedily
by a single group, with the optional newline plus more spaces folded
into one non-ambiguous alternative after it. Verified this produces
identical matches (and identical groups) as the old pattern on the
handful of valid reference-link shapes the tests already cover, and
added a dedicated regression test that fails on unmodified master and
passes with the fix.

Fixes #798.

commit.message:
Fix quadratic rendering time for many inline links (#1621)

Scanning from index 0 after every inline-pattern match rescanned the
unprocessed text repeatedly, making conversion quadratic in the number
of inline elements. Return the index just past the inserted placeholder
so the next scan starts at the unprocessed tail.

Fixes #1619.

commit.message:
Create AI Policy

The motivation for adopting this policy is to avoid wasting the maintainers'
time. We work on this project as volunteers and it is an unproductive waste of
time to interact with contributors who do not understand their contributions.

While we generaly would prefer to receive contributions which are not AI
generated, we understand that such tools can provide value in limited ways.
Therefore, we have attempted to create a policy which allows use of such tools
while also holding the contributor accountable. Hopefully this accomplishes our
goal. Closes #1610.

commit.message:
Fix infinite loop when text contains multiple unclosed comments

The `updatepos()` override was resetting the parser position to `0`,
causing infinite loops when multiple bogus/unclosed comments
appeared in the input (e.g., `</` or `<!--` followed by non-standard
characters). Now tracks the position of the triggering `<` and
advances past it instead of rewinding to the start of the buffer.

Fixes #1578.

* update changelog

commit.message:
Ensure nested elements inside inline comments are properly unescaped.

When inline Markdown elements are nested, each nested level contains its
own placeholder. Therefore, when unescaping, the regex substitution needs
to be run against each nested level. As this is nested inside the match, it ensures
no more than one non-matching regex will be run in each instance.

Closes #1571.
